```{r}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(baseballr)
library(ggridges)
```



```{r}
# get park data
ballparks_stadium_data <- read_csv("../../data/ballparks_stadium_data_2022.csv")
head(ballparks_stadium_data)
```

```{r}
ggplot(ballparks_stadium_data, aes(x = center_field, y = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

```{r}
# get downloaded hitter stats
`2022HitterStats` <- read_csv("../../data/2022HitterStats.csv")
head(`2022HitterStats`)
```


```{r}
# get player team info
Player_team_info <- mlb_stats(stat_type = 'season', stat_group = 'hitting', season = 2022) |>
  select(player_id, team_name, league_name)
```


```{r}
# join hitter stats with players team
Full_22_Hitter_stats <- `2022HitterStats` |>
  left_join(Player_team_info, join_by(player_id))

head(Full_22_Hitter_stats)
```

```{r}
# Some graphs that we could use (These need effective viz like alt caps, also feel free to do other effective viz aspects like coloring for improvement!)

#Density graph of On base % by different teams
ggplot(Full_22_Hitter_stats, aes(x = on_base_percent, y = team_name, fill = team_name)) +
  geom_density_ridges(scale = 2, alpha = 0.7, size = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "On Base %",
       y = "Team",
       title = "Distribution of OBP by Home Park (Ridgeline)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}

#|fig-alt: "Ridgeline plot showing the distribution of On-Base Percentage across different MLB teams for the 2022 season. Each team's density curve illustrates the spread of player OBP values, with color differentiation enhancing team distinction. Denser areas indicate where players' on-base percentages are more concentrated within a team"

ggplot(Full_22_Hitter_stats, aes(x = on_base_percent, y = reorder(team_name, on_base_percent), fill = team_name)) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    scale = 2.5, 
    alpha = 0.9, 
    size = 0.3, 
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.1, end = 0.9) +  # broader color range
  labs(
    x = "On-Base Percentage",
    y = "Team Name",
    title = "Distribution of On-Base Percentage by Team (2022 Season)",
    subtitle = "Ridgeline plot showing variability across teams",
    caption = "Source: 2022 MLB Hitter Stats"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "italic"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 8)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)  # make team names smaller to avoid overlapping
  )
```


```{r}
# join park stats and hitting stats
player_and_park_stats <- Full_22_Hitter_stats |>
  left_join(ballparks_stadium_data) 
```

```{r}
  ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = elevation)) +
      geom_point()
```

```{r}
ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = extra_distance)) +
  geom_point()
```


```{r}
ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = avg_temp)) +
  geom_point()
```



```{r}
#find which teams may have players more likely to over preform WOBA
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(wobadiff > 0) |>
  group_by(team_name) |>
  count() |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

```{r}
#find which team's players are likely to underpreform
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(wobadiff < 0) |>
  group_by(team_name) |>
  count() |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

```{r}
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(team_name %in%c ( "Cleveland Guardians", "Houston Astros	", "Houston Astros", "Los Angeles Dodgers", "New York Yankees", "New York Mets")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = team_name, size = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point() 
```

```{r}
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(team_name %in%c("Atlanta Braves", "Seattle Mariners", "Toronto Blue Jays")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = team_name, size = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point() 
```

```{r}
# Vis of teams with over six batters on the dataset
player_and_park_stats |>
  filter(team_name %in%c("Baltimore Orioles", "Houston Astros", "Los Angeles Dodgers", "New York Mets", "New York Yankees", "Seattle Mariners", "Toronto Blue Jays", "San Diego Padres")) |>
ggplot(aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = team_name, size = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
# Find what teams have enough players to be statistically significant
player_and_park_stats |>
  group_by(team_name) |>
  count() |>
  arrange(n)
```

```{r}
ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = woba, y = xwoba, color = hr_park_effects)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~league_name)
```

```{r}
player_and_park_stats |>
  group_by(league_name) |>
  summarise(mean(hr_park_effects))
```

```{r}
# difference in expected vs actual slugging compared to park effects
ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = hr_park_effects, y = xslgdiff)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# difference in expected vs actual weighted on base avreage compared to park effects
ggplot(player_and_park_stats, aes(x = hr_park_effects, y = wobadiff)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)
```
